group_scores.rationale: In-window RBI primary data shows rupee and liquidity strain: FX reserves fell $14.2bn in the week to 13 Nov (RBI-1, verified), the RBI moved from VRRR absorption on 17 Nov (RBI-3, verified) to oversubscribed VRR injection at 5.56-5.58% on 20 Nov, above the 5.50% repo rate (RBI-4 verified, RBI-5). All of it comes from one institution and is indirect. No T2 source confirms FPI outflows, a December hike or a named trigger for INDA's -6.04% relative fall. SEBI, USTR and the CBDT portal show no FPI tax, rule or tariff event in the window. A price move alone cannot set a score, so the default 0 stands.
group_scores.falsifier: -1 if NSDL shows heavy sustained FPI equity outflows over 14-20 Nov plus a T2 report naming a trigger or pricing a December MPC hike with the rupee weak; -1 or lower if an in-window CBDT or Finance Ministry notice raises FPI capital-gains tax or changes 115AD; +1 if T2 shows the rupee stabilising, FPI buying resuming and net MSCI passive inflows at the 30 Nov rebalance.

group_scores.rationale: The RBI strain is India-specific. The only in-window T2 EM fact, a record 17.5% weekly Taiex fall (TW-1, verified), goes against the reported EEM +3.75% vs world, and the gap is not explained. em_broad has fewer than 2 valid dated sources on any driver, so it stays at 0 with low confidence.
group_scores.falsifier: +1 if in-window T1 and T2 sources show EM ex-India flow or policy drivers (Korea, China, an MSCI review net inflow) behind EEM strength; -1 if a confirmed EM-wide driver appears (a strong dollar, an oil spike, the Taiwan AI-chip sell-off spreading, or FPI exits beyond India).
